//: The measured cell and pinned font for this machine, and the design system's own self-contradictions. A contradiction is a bug in .claude/design/, removed when the design is fixed upstream — never when the app changes. See crates/review/src/baseline.rs.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:232-241 closes the glyph table at `▌ ● ◐ ○ ✔ ▶ █ + -`, and IMPORT.md restates it as closed.
contradictions.design_also_says: The same document mandates `·` as the top bar's within-group separator (:142, :254-255), `→` on first run's `more` row (:336), `⏎` and `↑↓` in two footers (:280, :341), and presupposes `…` for clipping.
contradictions.app_follows: The copy. A frame cannot draw the screens the design specifies without these five marks, so the table is the half that is wrong.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:232-241's closed glyph table contains no box-drawing characters, and Turn 13's rule is that nothing inside a frame is stroked.
contradictions.design_also_says: The design system has no table component at all, and a one-dimensional ground ladder cannot express a two-dimensional grid of cell boundaries.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0002 — a markdown table in assistant prose is drawn with `┌ ┬ ┐ ├ ┼ ┤ └ ┴ ┘ ─ │`, scoped to that one construct. This entry is retired when the design system gains a table component.
